name: Retail / Merchandise

transitions.provenance: derived — GST-001 declares entryState.params  and GST-026 holds none of them. The edge carries nothing: GST-026 is opened from GST-001, so this edge is the way back and GST-001 keeps its own state
derived — GST-041 declares entryState.params holdId, lineId, performanceId, productId and GST-026 holds performanceId, so an edge into it carries them

notes:
States derived from the screen pattern on 17 August, not individually considered. Purpose derived from the screen name and its operations on 17 August, not from a requirement. **Cross-platform navigation removed 24 August**: BO-048, BO-069. **Buying to collect goes through the cart** (decided 28 September, audit R236) — `addCartLine`, `checkoutCart`, `createPayment`, and payment creates the shop-and-drop, as on the web's WEB-033; `reserveMerchandise` stays only as an unpaid hold to pay at the shop. **A till does not navigate to a back office and a guest app does not navigate to either** — those are device handovers, and a flow declares them with `crossesDevice` rather than a screen pretending there is a link.

**The unpaid hold stays secondary here, by decision (DEC-075, 2 October): paid only on the web (R236); the app's hold is drawn as secondary until decided.** A sanctioned difference from WEB-042 (CHG-SGU-018).
patternReason: `listMerchandise` reads the population and `getGameCard` reads one of them — list, select, act
purpose: Buy merchandise and collect it on the way out, or have it delivered home.

components.label: Merchandise
components.notes: The guest projection: name, photo, price and whether it can be bought; sold-out items stay visible. No sku, barcode, variant, stock or inventory ids.

components.label: Scan an item in the shop
components.notes: Sends `?outletId=` — the outlet the guest is browsing — because the app has no workstation; price and stock are that outlet's, and an inactive item is not found (decided 28 September, audit R215 (1)).

components.label: Hold to pay at the shop
components.notes: An unpaid hold, not a purchase — the item is allocated and paid for at the outlet; buying to collect is the cart above (decided 28 September, audit R236).

states.error: Could not load. Names which read failed and leaves the retail merchandise untouched.
states.emptyFirstRun: No retail merchandise yet. **Offers no create action** — this screen declares no operation that makes one — and says so rather than showing an empty table.
states.emptyNoResults: Nothing matches the filter on outletId, categoryId, inStockOnly, search and the retail merchandise are still there. Names the active filter and offers to clear it.
states.emptyNoAccess: **There is no permission to name: a guest holds none** (ADR-0025). The shop is public; buying needs the guest's cart.
states.offline: **The offline banner shows.** What was already loaded stays on screen, marked with its age. Anything that spends money, holds capacity or changes the account waits for the connection, and its button says so rather than failing.

apis.purpose: Find an item by code or scan
Put the item in the cart, marked for collection on the way out (audit R236)

entryState.coldEntry: **A guest arriving cold on a link that no longer resolves is shown what happened and one way onward — never a 404.** A shared ticket, a forwarded confirmation and a push notification opened three weeks late all land here, and the person holding the link did nothing wrong. **The screen names the thing, says it is expired, cancelled or withdrawn, and offers the list it came from.** Arrives with `cardCode`.

prototype.view: Account → All screens → Wave 2 → Retail / merchandise
prototype.differences: Prototype only reserves for collection (reserveMerchandise). The YAML also declares addCartLine/checkoutCart/createPayment and getGameCard, and the prototype shows neither a buy-now path nor a game card.

apisNote: Rebuilt 9 September 2026 from the 2 operations this screen declares, not from a workshop pack — it has none. Columns are every field the response schema declares, plumbing aside — narrowing them to the ones that matter is work a person still owes this screen.

overlays.body: The item and quantity, held to pay for at the shop until the end of the visit day (R169). No ids are asked.
The item and quantity (a size switches between sibling items); collection point or home delivery is chosen at checkout. No variant, performance or seat ids are asked.

offlineBanner.message: You're offline. Connect to the internet to book, pay, order or join a queue.
offlineBanner.shows: The moment the connection drops, on every screen, above the screen's own content.
offlineBanner.clears: By itself as soon as the connection is back, with a short "Back online" confirmation.
offlineBanner.never: Covers what is already on screen, or appears for a server error — that is the screen's own error state, and a guest told they are offline when the venue is down reconnects for nothing.
offlineBanner.provenance: Decided 12 September 2026 — guest web and guest app behave identically offline and say so with the same banner.

targetApp.name: TICVAI Guest
targetApp.note: **One guest product in three shells.** Web, mobile and kiosk share 73–91% of their operations; the kiosk is the same product in a fixed frame with no keyboard, and is deliberately narrower rather than different.
